>you want to use Java 1.7, you'll have to re-configure R for Java 1.7 and
>re-compile rJava to use those settings. Note hat Oracle's Java lives in
>an entirely different place

Acinonyx. I know my question is about JRI and not about JGR itself so I 
won't get upset if nobody answers.

Cheers,
Simon

Since Rserve is on the server, you can't use JavaGD in the typical sense as a visual display. There are a few options:

a) create the plot server-side and push it through Rserve. This is want most applications do since you have full freedom on the Java side. See PlotDemo.java in Rserve examples.

b) You could create a back-end for JavaGD that doesn't show the display but instead sends it to the client in some encoded form. You could simply serialize the GD objects for example.

c) use xGD package (https://www.rforge.net/xGD/ ) - it serializes graphics and there is a Java example unserializing it and displaying it. It is slightly older so if you decide to got that way, let me know and I'll see if it needs updates for the latests R.

It is stored in the "iplots:volatiles" environment. That environment is normally only accessible from iplots code so mortals are not supposed to know about it ;). But R is R after all so you can get at it using

> v=parent.env(parent.env(getNamespace("iplots")))
> v
<environment: 0x102a1bfc8>
attr(,"name")
[1] "volatiles:iplots"
> ls(,v,all=T)
[1] ".iplot.curid"    ".iplot.current"  ".iplots"         ".iplots.fw"     
[5] ".iset.selection" ".isets"          ".restricted.el" 

But you should not count on such a hack, as it is considered internal and thus can change without notice.

Cheers,
Simon

Hi Guys,
I'm trying to plug it into another Java app (imageJ), so I've plugged 
JGR into imageJ, hell of a fight but it works well.
So I'm trying to launch Deducer now, but when I do 
JGR.MAINRCONSOLE.execute(library(Deducer)) I get this Error message :

java.lang.UnsatisfiedLinkError: Native Library 
/home/musicien/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/2.15/rJava/jri/libjri.so 
already loaded in another classloader
     at java.lang.ClassLoader.loadLibrary1(ClassLoader.java:1901)
     at java.lang.ClassLoader.loadLibrary0(ClassLoader.java:1860)
     at java.lang.ClassLoader.loadLibrary(ClassLoader.java:1834)
     at java.lang.Runtime.loadLibrary0(Runtime.java:845)
     at java.lang.System.loadLibrary(System.java:1084)
     at org.rosuda.JRI.Rengine.<clinit>(Rengine.java:19)
     at java.lang.Class.forName0(Native Method)
     at java.lang.Class.forName(Class.java:266)
     at org.rosuda.JRI.Rengine.rniRunMainLoop(Native Method)
     at org.rosuda.JRI.Rengine.run(Rengine.java:640)

Ian Fellows answered and the problem is that we can't make two different 
loads of the same Library. Is there a way to avoid that?
I found that It was not possible to unload a Java library from the Java VM.
But is must be possible to add a condition to check if the library is 
already loaded before "re-loading" it. I found this :
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/1007861/how-do-i-get-a-list-of-jni-libraries-which-are-loaded/1008631#1008631
Is there a way to "modify" this? I searched in the source code of JRI 
and Deducer and couldn't find where the library was loaded.
Thanks.

I made a post on Deducer googlegroup. Ian Fellows answer is here :

Subject: 	Re: Plugging JGR into a Java app and launch Deducer
Date: 	Tue, 16 Apr 2013 09:35:02 -0700
From: 	Ian Fellows <ifellows at gmail.com>
Reply-To: 	deducer at googlegroups.com
To: 	deducer at googlegroups.com



This question is probably better suited to the rosuda devel list. The 
problem is that you have two java classloaders running at the same time. 
the usual one started by ImageJ, and the one started from within R by 
rJava.

I don't know of a solution to this issue. usually java programs are 
either embedded within R (as in Deducer), or embed R within them. What 
you are trying to do is both.


best,
Ian

Typically, it's the key between <Ctrl> and <Alt>, but on Linux users sometimes re-map it to other keys (see below).


> ), thus, for

All bets are off on Linux. The mapping in X11 is arbitrarily changeable by the user and I'm not even sure what we support there - key handling is incomplete for X11 AFAIR. I'll be happy to incorporate patches from volunteers.
The above description applies to Mac OS X. On Windows there is an issue with <Meta> as the OS tends to grab it for its own purpose, but then Windows users typically have the middle mouse button so they don't need <Meta>.

Cheers,
Simon
